questions.explain: Bài không nêu công trình Brutalist nổi tiếng nhất hay vị trí của nó → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why did the buildings decline in popularity by the 1980s?
options: They were deemed too expensive to build.
They were badly maintained and weathered unattractively.
They were abandoned by architects after construction.
They were considered unsafe for occupants.
questions.explain: Bài viết: bê tông phong hóa không đều, nhiều tòa nhà ít được bảo trì khi sự lạc quan đã tan biến → đáp án đúng: They were badly maintained and weathered unattractively.

questions.q: What does the writer conclude from the history of Brutalism?
options: Modern architects lack skill.
Old buildings should always be preserved.
Concrete should never be used again.
Aesthetic judgements can change over time.
questions.explain: Bài viết: tòa nhà không đổi nhưng phán xét có thể đảo ngược trong một thế hệ → đáp án đúng: Aesthetic judgements can change over time.

readings.title: Moral Luck
readings.summaryVi: Nghịch lý "may rủi đạo đức": ta đánh giá con người theo hậu quả họ không kiểm soát được, dù ta tin rằng chỉ những gì kiểm soát được mới đáng bị khen trách.
readings.summaryEn: The paradox of "moral luck": we judge people by outcomes beyond their control, even though we believe only what is under control deserves praise or blame.
readings.text:
Consider two drivers who are equally tired and equally careless. One reaches home unscathed; the other, through no fault of his own timing, strikes a child who steps into the road. Almost everyone judges the second driver more harshly, and he will probably judge himself more harshly too. Yet the only difference between them is luck, and a principle many of us hold dear says that people should be assessed only for what lies within their control.

This is the puzzle that the philosophers Thomas Nagel and Bernard Williams brought to prominence under the label moral luck. The tension is stubborn because both intuitions seem compelling. If we abandon the principle of control, we must accept that people may be blamed for outcomes they could not have foreseen. If we adhere to it, we must say that the two drivers are equally culpable, a verdict that sits uneasily with the visceral horror we feel at the child's death.

Some philosophers resolve the conflict by denying the data, insisting that our reactions to outcomes are mere emotion rather than moral judgement. Others accept that responsibility has several dimensions: the drivers may be equally blameworthy for their carelessness but not equally responsible for what followed, and the second may owe compensation or an apology that the first does not. Whether such distinctions dissolve the paradox or merely relabel it remains contested, which is perhaps why the problem has endured.

questions.q: The two drivers in the example behave in equally careless ways.
questions.explain: Bài viết: cả hai tài xế "equally tired and equally careless" → TRUE.

questions.q: Nagel and Williams agreed completely on how to solve the problem of moral luck.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói hai ông đưa vấn đề này lên hàng đầu, không nói họ có cùng giải pháp hay không → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: The writer claims that the paradox of moral luck has been fully solved.
questions.explain: Bài viết: liệu các phân biệt có hóa giải nghịch lý hay chỉ đổi tên nó "remains contested" (còn tranh cãi) → FALSE.

questions.q: What principle makes the situation puzzling?
options: People should be judged only for what they control.
Negligent behavior must be penalized in every case.
Innocent victims should never bear responsibility.
Random events are fundamentally impossible to quantify.
questions.explain: Bài viết: nguyên tắc nhiều người coi trọng là con người chỉ nên bị đánh giá về những gì "within their control" → đáp án đúng: People should be judged only for what they control.

questions.q: How do some philosophers try to resolve the conflict?
options: By abolishing the idea of responsibility
By distinguishing different dimensions of responsibility
By proving that luck does not exist
By treating both drivers identically in every respect
questions.explain: Bài viết: trách nhiệm có nhiều chiều, hai tài xế có thể đáng trách như nhau về sự bất cẩn nhưng không chịu trách nhiệm như nhau về hậu quả → đáp án đúng: By distinguishing different dimensions of responsibility.

readings.title: The Slow Failure of Antibiotics
readings.summaryVi: Kháng kháng sinh là hệ quả tất yếu của chọn lọc tự nhiên; vấn đề thật sự nằm ở kinh tế học: thuốc mới ít sinh lời, nên cần cơ chế khuyến khích mới.
readings.summaryEn: Antibiotic resistance is the inevitable result of natural selection; the real problem is economic: new drugs earn little, so new incentives are needed.
readings.text:
When Alexander Fleming noticed in 1928 that a mould had killed the bacteria around it, he inaugurated an era in which infections that had been routinely fatal became trivial to treat. Less than a century later, that era is under threat. Resistance is not a malfunction but an inevitable consequence of natural selection: when a population of bacteria is exposed to an antibiotic, the few individuals that happen to carry protective mutations survive and multiply, and the drug gradually loses its force.

Every use of an antibiotic accelerates this process, and many uses are unnecessary. Antibiotics are prescribed for viral illnesses on which they have no effect, taken for incomplete courses, and administered in vast quantities to livestock to promote growth. Resistant strains then travel readily across borders, so that careless prescribing in one country becomes everyone's problem.

Scientific ingenuity alone will not resolve the matter, because the obstacle is largely economic. A new antibiotic that is held in reserve for the most dangerous infections, precisely as stewardship demands, will sell in small volumes, while a drug for a chronic condition taken daily for decades is far more lucrative. Several large companies have consequently withdrawn from the field. Proposals to remedy this include paying developers a fixed annual sum for access to a new drug irrespective of how much of it is used, thereby separating revenue from volume. Such schemes are costly, but the alternative, a return to a world in which minor surgery carries mortal risk, would be costlier still.

questions.q: Bacterial resistance to antibiotics results from natural selection.
questions.explain: Bài viết: kháng thuốc là "an inevitable consequence of natural selection" → TRUE.

questions.q: Antibiotics are effective against most viral illnesses when taken for a full course.
questions.explain: Bài viết: kháng sinh bị kê cho bệnh do virus "on which they have no effect" → FALSE.

questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói Fleming quan sát được năm 1928, không nhắc giải Nobel → NOT GIVEN.

options: Bacterial strains have become too complex for current laboratory methods.
Regulators have barred the commercial sale of new antibiotics.
New antibiotics are used sparingly and so earn little.
Livestock producers choose older drugs over newly developed antibiotics.
questions.explain: Bài viết: thuốc kháng sinh mới được giữ dự trữ nên "will sell in small volumes", kém sinh lời hơn thuốc bệnh mạn tính → đáp án đúng: New antibiotics are used sparingly and so earn little.

options: Lower the cost of antibiotics for agricultural producers
Declare antibiotic resistance a criminal offense under law
Replace antibiotics with vaccines
Separate developers' income from the quantity of drug sold

readings.title: Why We Still Read Novels
readings.summaryVi: Tiểu thuyết bị tuyên bố là "sắp chết" nhiều lần nhưng vẫn tồn tại vì nó cho ta trải nghiệm hiếm có: sống trong ý thức của người khác trong thời gian dài.
readings.summaryEn: The novel has been declared dying many times yet survives because it offers a rare experience: inhabiting another consciousness at length.
readings.text:
The death of the novel has been announced with such regularity that the announcement has become a literary genre in its own right. Cinema was supposed to kill it, then television, then the internet; each, in turn, has failed to do so. The persistence of a form so demanding of time and attention, in an age of limitless distraction, invites explanation.

One answer lies in what the novel does uniquely well. A film can show what a character does and, with a skilful actor, what he seems to feel. Only prose can render the continuous, self-contradicting texture of consciousness itself: the half-formed thought, the memory that interrupts a conversation, the gap between what a person says and what she means. To read a long novel is to live inside another mind for days, an intimacy that few other media can match.

Some researchers claim that this immersion has measurable benefits, citing studies in which readers of literary fiction perform slightly better on tests of empathy. The findings, however, have proved difficult to replicate, and it would be unwise to treat them as settled. A more modest claim may be sturdier: that the novel trains a certain kind of patience, an ability to withhold judgement while a perspective unfolds. Whether or not it makes us better people, it makes us, at the very least, more attentive ones, and that would be quite enough to justify its survival.

questions.q: Announcements of the death of the novel have been very frequent.
questions.explain: Bài viết: lời tuyên bố được lặp lại "with such regularity" đến mức thành một thể loại văn học → TRUE.

questions.q: The writer considers the studies on literary fiction and empathy to be fully reliable.
questions.explain: Bài viết: các phát hiện "difficult to replicate" và "unwise to treat them as settled" → FALSE.

questions.q: Most novel readers today are under thirty.
questions.explain: Bài không cung cấp thông tin về tuổi của độc giả → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: According to the writer, what can prose do that film cannot easily do?
options: Tell a longer story
Represent the texture of a mind's inner life
Reach a wider audience
Entertain without effort
questions.explain: Bài viết: chỉ văn xuôi mới "render the continuous, self-contradicting texture of consciousness itself" → đáp án đúng: Represent the texture of a mind's inner life.

questions.q: What is the writer's own view of the benefits of reading novels?
options: They probably encourage patience and attentiveness.
They definitely improve readers' vocabulary skills.
They replace the need for any other narrative forms.
They are mainly useful for teaching grammar rules.

readings.title: Flexibility at a Price
readings.summaryVi: Nền kinh tế "gig" hứa hẹn tự do nhưng chuyển rủi ro từ doanh nghiệp sang người lao động; tranh luận pháp lý xoay quanh việc họ là nhân viên hay người làm tự do.
readings.summaryEn: The gig economy promises autonomy but shifts risk from companies to workers; the legal debate turns on whether they are employees or contractors.
readings.text:
The platforms that connect drivers, couriers and freelancers with customers through a smartphone have been celebrated as engines of flexibility. Workers choose their hours; customers enjoy convenience; companies avoid the overheads of a permanent workforce. It is an arrangement in which, at first sight, everyone gains.

On closer inspection, the advantages are unevenly distributed. Because gig workers are classified as independent contractors, they typically have no entitlement to sick pay, holiday pay or a minimum wage, and they bear the costs of vehicles, fuel and insurance themselves. The platform, meanwhile, retains considerable control: it sets prices, monitors performance through ratings and may suspend accounts without explanation. A worker who is nominally free to decline a job but penalised for doing so enjoys a freedom of a rather theoretical kind.

Courts in several countries have been asked to determine whether this classification reflects reality. Some have ruled that, where a company directs the work in substance, the people performing it are entitled to the protections of employment; others have upheld the contractor model. Companies argue that reclassification would destroy the flexibility that workers value and reduce the number of jobs available.

There is likely to be no single answer. A student earning supplementary income on weekends has different needs from a parent who depends on the platform for her livelihood. The more productive debate may concern not the label but the floor of protection beneath all work, whatever the label happens to be.

questions.q: Gig workers usually pay for their own vehicles and insurance.
questions.explain: Bài viết: họ "bear the costs of vehicles, fuel and insurance themselves" → TRUE.

questions.q: All courts that have considered the issue have decided that gig workers are employees.
questions.explain: Bài viết: một số tòa phán quyết như vậy, nhưng "others have upheld the contractor model" → FALSE.

questions.q: The majority of gig workers in Europe earn less than the minimum wage.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói họ thường không có quyền hưởng lương tối thiểu, không đưa tỉ lệ thu nhập dưới mức đó → NOT GIVEN.

options: Workers are enthusiastic about abstract concepts.
Freedom means the same as schedule flexibility.
Workers can refuse jobs only at a cost.
Workers cannot decide their own working hours.

questions.q: What is the writer's view at the end of the passage?
options: Platforms should be banned.
The label matters more than anything else.
Gig work is better than permanent employment.
The basic protections for all work matter more than the label.
questions.explain: Bài viết: cuộc tranh luận hiệu quả hơn nên bàn về "the floor of protection beneath all work, whatever the label" → đáp án đúng: The basic protections for all work matter more than the label.

readings.title: The Last Speakers
readings.summaryVi: Một nửa trong khoảng bảy nghìn ngôn ngữ trên thế giới có thể biến mất trong thế kỷ này; vấn đề không chỉ là mất từ vựng mà còn là mất cả kho tri thức bản địa.
readings.summaryEn: Perhaps half of the world's roughly seven thousand languages may vanish this century; what is lost is not only vocabulary but whole stores of local knowledge.
readings.text:
Of the roughly seven thousand languages spoken today, linguists estimate that as many as half will fall silent before the century is out. Languages do not typically perish through persecution, although that has happened; more commonly they decline because parents, judging that a dominant language offers their children better prospects, cease to pass on their own. Within a generation, a community's mother tongue can shrink to a handful of elderly speakers.

The loss is sometimes dismissed as sentimental. If the speakers are bilingual, the argument goes, nothing practical is forfeited. This overlooks the fact that languages are repositories of knowledge accumulated over centuries. Speakers of a small Amazonian language may possess a classification of medicinal plants that no botanist has recorded; a Pacific island vocabulary may encode generations of observation of tides and fish migration. When the last fluent speaker dies, such understanding frequently goes with her.

Revival efforts offer cautious grounds for hope. Hebrew, once confined to liturgy, was reborn as an everyday language, and Welsh and Maori have been strengthened through immersion schools and broadcasting. Success, however, demands more than goodwill: it requires that children encounter the language in settings that matter to them, and that speaking it carries social rewards rather than stigma. Without these, even generously funded programmes tend to produce speakers who can recite but not converse. A language survives not in archives but in the mouths of the young.

questions.q: Most languages disappear because speakers are forbidden to use them.
questions.explain: Bài viết: ngôn ngữ ít khi mất do đàn áp; thường là do cha mẹ không truyền lại ("more commonly they decline because parents ... cease to pass on their own") → FALSE.

questions.q: Some small languages contain detailed knowledge of the natural environment.
questions.explain: Bài viết nêu ngôn ngữ Amazon với phân loại cây thuốc và ngôn ngữ đảo Thái Bình Dương với quan sát thủy triều, cá → TRUE.

questions.q: Why do some people regard the loss of languages as unimportant?
options: They believe bilingual speakers lose nothing practical.
They assume new tongues spread faster than old ones.
They argue scholars overstate the extinction rates.
They value oral traditions over texts.
questions.explain: Bài viết: lập luận là nếu người nói song ngữ thì "nothing practical is forfeited" → đáp án đúng: They believe bilingual speakers lose nothing practical.

questions.q: According to the writer, what does revival need above all?
options: Providing large financial endowments to language projects alone
Compiling extensive written grammars without community use
Children using the language in meaningful settings
Using foreign government aid without involving the community

readings.title: Why Music Moves Us
readings.summaryVi: Âm nhạc gây cảm xúc mạnh dù không có chức năng sinh tồn rõ ràng; một giả thuyết cho rằng nó vận hành bằng cách tạo rồi thỏa mãn hoặc trì hoãn những kỳ vọng.
readings.summaryEn: Music provokes strong emotion despite having no obvious survival function; one theory holds that it works by creating, and then fulfilling or delaying, expectations.
readings.text:
That a sequence of organised sounds can bring a person to tears or raise the hairs on the back of her neck is, from an evolutionary perspective, odd. Unlike food or sex, music satisfies no evident biological need, yet every known human society makes it. Theories abound: that it facilitated bonding in early groups, that it grew out of the intonation of speech, or that it is a by-product of other cognitive faculties, a kind of "auditory cheesecake" that happens to tickle pleasure circuits designed for other purposes.

A more empirical line of inquiry concerns how music produces feeling. The composer and theorist Leonard Meyer argued that emotion in music arises from expectation. As we listen, we continually predict what will come next, drawing on a lifetime's exposure to the conventions of our culture. When the prediction is confirmed, we feel satisfaction; when it is thwarted, we feel surprise; and when resolution is withheld for a while and then granted, the effect can be exhilarating. Brain-imaging studies have found that moments of anticipation before a favourite passage trigger the release of dopamine, the neurotransmitter associated with reward.

This account has the merit of explaining why unfamiliar traditions can initially sound strange or even unpleasant: our predictive machinery has not been trained on them. It also explains why the greatest music rarely does what we expect, but does something we recognise, immediately afterwards, as inevitable.

questions.q: Every known human society produces music.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "every known human society makes it" → TRUE.

questions.q: Leonard Meyer believed that musical emotion has nothing to do with expectation.
questions.explain: Bài viết: Meyer cho rằng cảm xúc trong âm nhạc "arises from expectation" → FALSE.

questions.q: Musicians show stronger dopamine responses than non-musicians.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói giai đoạn chờ đợi trước đoạn nhạc yêu thích kích hoạt dopamine, không so sánh nhạc sĩ với người thường → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What does "auditory cheesecake" refer to?
options: A traditional folk melody performed at celebrations in rural communities
A pleasant by-product of faculties that evolved for other purposes
A rare auditory disorder affecting pitch perception in some individuals
A kind of musical instrument used in orchestras
questions.explain: Đó là cách nói ví von: âm nhạc là "by-product of other cognitive faculties" làm thỏa mãn các mạch khoái cảm → đáp án đúng: A pleasant by-product of faculties that evolved for other purposes.

questions.q: How does the expectation theory explain why unfamiliar music may sound strange?
options: The instruments used are unfamiliar to most listeners.
The recording quality is poor and distorts the sound.
The rhythms follow patterns that are unusually complex.
Listeners lack the habits needed to predict it.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "our predictive machinery has not been trained on them" → đáp án đúng: Listeners lack the habits needed to predict it.

readings.title: Cities Under Heat
readings.summaryVi: Đô thị nóng hơn vùng nông thôn quanh nó; giải pháp như cây xanh và mái nhà sáng màu hiệu quả nhưng chỉ thành công nếu đặt đúng nơi dễ tổn thương nhất.
readings.summaryEn: Cities run hotter than the countryside around them; remedies such as trees and pale roofs work, but only when directed to the most vulnerable neighbourhoods.
readings.text:
On a still summer night, the centre of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside. This urban heat island effect arises because dark surfaces such as asphalt and roofing absorb sunlight by day and release it slowly after dusk, because buildings obstruct the wind that would otherwise carry heat away, and because air conditioners, vehicles and industry add heat of their own. As global temperatures climb, the effect compounds the danger of heatwaves, which already kill more people in many countries than any other weather event.

The remedies are well understood. Trees shade pavements and cool the air through evaporation; pale roofs and road surfaces reflect sunlight; green roofs and parks provide refuges. Experiments suggest that a determined programme of planting and resurfacing can lower local temperatures by a degree or two, a modest figure with a considerable effect on mortality.

What matters, however, is where the effort goes. Heat is distributed with a striking inequity: poorer districts typically have fewer trees, more paving and less access to cooling, so that the residents with the least capacity to adapt endure the highest temperatures. Planting in already leafy suburbs, however attractive, does little for those at greatest risk. The technical problem of cooling a city is, in short, easier than the political one of deciding who should be cooled first, and cities that answer the second question honestly are likely to save the most lives.

questions.q: Dark surfaces in cities release stored heat slowly after sunset.
questions.explain: Bài viết: bề mặt tối "absorb sunlight by day and release it slowly after dusk" → TRUE.

questions.q: Planting trees can lower temperatures by about ten degrees across an entire city.
questions.explain: Bài viết: chương trình trồng cây và lát lại đường có thể giảm nhiệt "by a degree or two", một con số khiêm tốn → FALSE.

questions.q: Air conditioning has been banned in several cities because of its heat output.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ nói điều hòa góp thêm nhiệt, không nhắc đến lệnh cấm → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: According to the passage, why are poorer districts more at risk?
options: They contain more factories.
They have fewer trees and less cooling.
They are located closer to the coast.
They have older residents only.
questions.explain: Bài viết: khu nghèo thường "fewer trees, more paving and less access to cooling" → đáp án đúng: They have fewer trees and less cooling.

questions.q: What is the writer's main argument in the last paragraph?
options: The political decision of whom to help first is the harder part.
The technical challenge of cooling a city is already solved.
The financial benefit of planting trees in suburbs outweighs other measures.
The inevitability of heatwaves makes any mitigation effort pointless.
questions.explain: Bài viết: vấn đề kỹ thuật dễ hơn "the political one of deciding who should be cooled first" → đáp án đúng: The political decision of whom to help first is the harder part.

readings.title: Falsification and Its Discontents
readings.summaryVi: Tiêu chí "có thể bác bỏ" của Popper là chuẩn mực hấp dẫn để phân định khoa học, nhưng các nhà triết học chỉ ra rằng thực tế nghiên cứu phức tạp hơn một phép thử đơn giản.
readings.summaryEn: Popper's criterion of falsifiability is an appealing yardstick for science, but philosophers point out that real research is more tangled than any single test.
readings.text:
Ask a scientist what distinguishes science from pseudoscience and the chances are she will invoke Karl Popper. Popper observed that no quantity of confirming instances can prove a universal claim, since the next observation might contradict it, whereas a single counterexample can refute it. Genuine theories, he concluded, are those that forbid certain outcomes and so expose themselves to refutation; a doctrine that can accommodate any evidence whatsoever, as he thought certain schools of psychoanalysis could, is not thereby strong but empty.

The criterion has a bracing clarity, and it has served as a useful corrective against theories that explain everything and therefore nothing. Yet historians and philosophers have argued that it misdescribes how research proceeds. When an experiment contradicts a theory, scientists rarely discard the theory forthwith. They may suspect the instrument, the sample or an auxiliary assumption, and they are often right to do so. The discovery of the planet Neptune is the classic illustration: astronomers who found Uranus straying from its predicted orbit did not abandon Newtonian mechanics but posited an unseen planet, and were vindicated.

The more defensible conclusion is that falsifiability is a virtue rather than a rule. A theory that can never in principle be tested deserves suspicion, but the verdict on any particular theory emerges from a web of evidence, auxiliary assumptions and competing explanations, not from a single decisive experiment. Science, it seems, is messier than its philosophers, and rather more successful.

questions.q: Popper argued that many confirming observations can prove a universal claim.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "no quantity of confirming instances can prove a universal claim" → FALSE.

questions.q: The discovery of Neptune is used to show that scientists sometimes keep a theory despite contradicting evidence.
questions.explain: Các nhà thiên văn không bỏ cơ học Newton mà giả định một hành tinh chưa thấy rồi được chứng minh đúng → TRUE.

questions.q: Popper wrote his main work on falsification while living in exile.
questions.explain: Bài không cho biết hoàn cảnh sống của Popper khi viết tác phẩm → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What is the writer's main criticism of Popper's criterion?
options: It is too difficult to understand.
It favours psychology over physics.
It ignores the way scientists actually handle contradictory results.
It has been proved wrong by Neptune.
questions.explain: Bài viết: tiêu chí này "misdescribes how research proceeds", vì nhà khoa học hiếm khi bỏ ngay lý thuyết khi gặp kết quả trái ngược → đáp án đúng: It ignores the way scientists actually handle contradictory results.

questions.q: What does the writer mean by saying falsifiability is "a virtue rather than a rule"?
options: It is mandated by official statutes and regulations
It should be completely disregarded in scientific research
It applies exclusively within the discipline of physics
It is a desirable quality but not an absolute test.
questions.explain: Lý thuyết không thể kiểm chứng đáng ngờ, nhưng phán quyết đến từ cả mạng lưới bằng chứng chứ không từ một thí nghiệm quyết định → đáp án đúng: It is a desirable quality but not an absolute test.

readings.title: The Price of Attention
readings.summaryVi: Các nền tảng miễn phí kiếm tiền bằng cách bán sự chú ý của người dùng; thiết kế để giữ chân gây ra câu hỏi về quyền tự quyết, nhưng cũng cần tránh lối kể chuyện hoảng loạn.
readings.summaryEn: Free platforms earn money by selling users' attention; designing to hold it raises questions about autonomy, though panicky narratives should also be avoided.
readings.text:
The business model of many digital services can be summarised in an adage: if you are not paying for the product, you are the product. More precisely, what is sold to advertisers is not the user but her attention, and the longer a platform can hold it, the more revenue it earns. This simple incentive has shaped the architecture of the apps on which a large part of the world now spends its waking hours: infinite scrolling, autoplaying videos and notifications calibrated to summon a lapsed user back.

Critics contend that these features exploit psychological vulnerabilities, particularly the susceptibility of human beings to intermittent rewards, the same principle that makes slot machines compelling. Defenders reply that people are not helpless: they can switch off alerts, set limits and walk away, and the services provide real value, from keeping families in touch to disseminating knowledge.

Both positions contain truth, and the evidence on harm is less conclusive than headlines suggest. Large studies have found associations between heavy use and poorer wellbeing, particularly among adolescents, but the effects are small on average and the direction of causation is disputed: unhappy people may turn to screens as much as screens make people unhappy.

Where the critique is strongest is not in its claims about addiction but in its observation about asymmetry. Behind every screen stand teams of engineers testing thousands of variations to see what retains users, while the individual brings only her willpower. Regulating the most manipulative techniques, such as design that makes cancelling a subscription deliberately arduous, is therefore less a matter of paternalism than of levelling an uneven contest.

questions.q: According to the passage, advertisers are buying the attention of users.
questions.explain: Bài viết: thứ được bán cho nhà quảng cáo "is not the user but her attention" → TRUE.

questions.q: The writer states that large studies have proved that social media causes unhappiness.
questions.explain: Bài viết: tác động nhỏ và "the direction of causation is disputed" → FALSE.

questions.q: Slot machine manufacturers have helped design some social media features.
questions.explain: Bài chỉ so sánh nguyên lý phần thưởng ngắt quãng giống máy đánh bạc, không nói có sự hợp tác thiết kế → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: What do defenders of the platforms argue?
options: Users are not helpless and receive real benefits.
Notifications never cause any negative effects for users.
Adolescents are required to avoid using these platforms.
All advertising on the platforms must be completely removed.
questions.explain: Bài viết: người ta có thể tắt thông báo, đặt giới hạn, và dịch vụ mang giá trị thật → đáp án đúng: Users are not helpless and receive real benefits.

questions.q: According to the writer, where is the critique of the platforms strongest?
options: In its claims about addiction
In its claims about advertising revenue
In its observation that the contest between engineers and individuals is unequal
In its predictions about teenagers
questions.explain: Bài viết: điểm mạnh nhất là nhận xét về "asymmetry": đội kỹ sư thử hàng nghìn biến thể còn cá nhân chỉ có ý chí → đáp án đúng: In its observation that the contest between engineers and individuals is unequal.

readings.title: The Unreliable Witness
readings.summaryVi: Trí nhớ không phải bản ghi mà là sự tái dựng nên dễ bị nhiễu; lời khai nhân chứng tự tin chưa chắc chính xác, dẫn đến cải cách thẩm vấn và nhận diện nghi phạm.
readings.summaryEn: Memory is a reconstruction, not a recording, and so is prone to distortion; a confident eyewitness is not necessarily an accurate one, prompting reforms in questioning and line-ups.
readings.text:
Popular intuition holds that memory resembles a video camera that, with sufficient prompting, can replay the past. Decades of experimental work suggest something closer to the opposite. Remembering is an act of reconstruction: the mind assembles fragments of what was perceived and fills the gaps with inference and expectation, and the result feels vivid whether or not it is accurate.

The psychologist Elizabeth Loftus demonstrated how easily the process can be nudged. In her classic experiments, participants who watched footage of a collision and were then asked how fast the cars were going when they "smashed into" one another gave higher estimates than those asked about cars that had "hit", and a week later were more likely to recall broken glass that had not been there. Subtle wording, it seemed, could alter the memory itself rather than merely the report of it.

These findings have unsettling implications for courtrooms, where an eyewitness's confident identification can be decisive. Analyses of cases in which convicted people were later exonerated by DNA evidence have repeatedly found that mistaken identification played a part. Confidence, crucially, is a poor guide to accuracy, especially when it has been inflated by feedback after the event.

Reforms have followed. Many police forces now present suspects sequentially rather than in a group, record the witness's confidence immediately, and avoid leading questions. None of this implies that witnesses lie, merely that honesty and accuracy are different things, and that a system relying on the second should not assume it from the first.

questions.q: The writer says that memory works like a video camera.
questions.explain: Bài viết bác quan niệm đó: nghiên cứu cho thấy điều "closer to the opposite", trí nhớ là sự tái dựng → FALSE.

questions.q: In Loftus's experiments, the choice of verb influenced the speed estimates.
questions.explain: Bài viết: người được hỏi với "smashed into" đưa ra ước tính tốc độ cao hơn người được hỏi với "hit" → TRUE.

questions.q: Most eyewitnesses who identify the wrong person are deliberately lying.
questions.explain: Bài viết: "None of this implies that witnesses lie" (không nói nhân chứng nói dối) → FALSE.

questions.q: Why is confidence a poor guide to accuracy?
options: Because confident people never make mistakes
Because it can be inflated by later feedback
Because it is difficult to measure
Because it is lower in older witnesses
questions.explain: Bài viết: độ tự tin có thể bị thổi phồng "by feedback after the event" → đáp án đúng: Because it can be inflated by later feedback.

questions.q: Which reform is mentioned in the passage?
options: Banning eyewitness evidence
Showing witnesses video footage
Interviewing witnesses after a week
Presenting suspects one at a time
questions.explain: Bài viết: nhiều lực lượng cảnh sát "present suspects sequentially rather than in a group" → đáp án đúng: Presenting suspects one at a time.

readings.title: Is Growth Everything?
readings.summaryVi: GDP đo sản lượng chứ không đo phúc lợi; các nhà kinh tế bất đồng về việc tăng trưởng có thể tách khỏi tác động môi trường hay không, và nên đo gì thay thế.
readings.summaryEn: GDP measures output, not wellbeing; economists disagree on whether growth can be decoupled from environmental damage and on what should replace it as a yardstick.
readings.text:
For three-quarters of a century, gross domestic product has served as the principal scoreboard of national success. Its appeal is obvious: it is a single figure, computed consistently, that rises when more is produced and sold. Yet its architects never intended it as a measure of wellbeing, and its shortcomings are well documented. It counts the cost of cleaning up an oil spill as an addition to output, ignores unpaid labour such as caring for relatives, and is indifferent to how income is distributed.

Such objections have prompted a search for alternatives, from indices that incorporate health and education to surveys of life satisfaction. These are illuminating but have not displaced GDP, partly because they are harder to compare and easier to manipulate.

A deeper controversy concerns whether growth is compatible with environmental limits. Advocates of "green growth" contend that output can be decoupled from resource use through efficiency and clean technology, and they point to countries whose emissions have fallen while their economies have expanded. Sceptics reply that such reductions are too slow and too small, partly because production is often simply exported to other countries, and that infinite expansion on a finite planet is a contradiction.

The evidence permits no easy verdict. What can be said is that the choice is not between growth and its abandonment but between kinds of growth, and that a society which cannot say what it is trying to achieve will find any measure inadequate.

questions.q: GDP was originally designed to measure the wellbeing of citizens.
questions.explain: Bài viết: những người xây dựng GDP "never intended it as a measure of wellbeing" → FALSE.

questions.q: GDP counts the cost of cleaning up an oil spill as part of output.
questions.explain: Bài viết: GDP "counts the cost of cleaning up an oil spill as an addition to output" → TRUE.

questions.q: Surveys of life satisfaction have been adopted by every government as the main measure of success.
questions.explain: Bài viết: các chỉ số thay thế "have not displaced GDP" → FALSE.

questions.q: Why do sceptics doubt that green growth is working?
options: Clean technology is still theoretical and has yet to be deployed at scale worldwide.
Emission cuts are too small and slow, and production may simply be moved abroad.
Some economists claim that global economies have reached a plateau and can no longer grow.
Consumers often choose cheaper items, refusing to buy products labeled as energy‑saving.
questions.explain: Bài viết: mức giảm "too slow and too small", và sản xuất thường chỉ được xuất sang nước khác → đáp án đúng: Emission cuts are too small and slow, and production may simply be moved abroad.

questions.q: What does the writer conclude?
options: Growth should be completely abandoned by all nations
GDP is regarded as the perfect economic measure
The real issue is what kind of growth a society wants.
Alternatives to GDP are considered impossible to develop
questions.explain: Bài viết: lựa chọn không phải giữa tăng trưởng và từ bỏ nó mà giữa "kinds of growth" → đáp án đúng: The real issue is what kind of growth a society wants.

readings.title: The Office Reconsidered
readings.summaryVi: Làm việc từ xa đem lại tự chủ và tiết kiệm thời gian đi lại nhưng làm yếu tương tác ngẫu nhiên và việc học nghề của người mới; mô hình kết hợp đang được thử nghiệm.
readings.summaryEn: Remote work brings autonomy and saved commuting time but weakens chance encounters and newcomers' learning on the job; hybrid models are being tested.
readings.text:
Before 2020, remote work was an occasional perk granted to trusted employees. Within a matter of weeks, it became the norm for millions, and the surprise was how smoothly many organisations adapted. Productivity, by most measures, held up, and employees welcomed the savings in time and money that came from abolishing the daily commute.

As the novelty faded, however, the drawbacks became clearer. Much of what happens in an office is unplanned: a casual remark overheard at a neighbouring desk, a quick question put to a colleague in a corridor. Such exchanges are rarely recorded in any plan, yet they transmit tacit knowledge and cement relationships. Junior staff, who learn largely by observing others, appear to lose most from their absence, and managers report that mentoring is harder to sustain through a screen.

Hybrid arrangements, in which employees spend part of the week on site, have emerged as a compromise, but they bring complications of their own. If colleagues choose different days, the office may be empty precisely when it was meant to be useful; if attendance is mandated, those who prized flexibility may leave.

The most successful firms seem to be those that treat the question as one of purpose rather than policy. They ask what particular activities, such as onboarding, brainstorming or resolving conflict, genuinely benefit from being in the same room, and design their schedules around them, rather than defending a location for its own sake.

questions.q: Productivity fell sharply when many people began working from home.
questions.explain: Bài viết: năng suất "by most measures, held up" (nhìn chung được giữ vững) → FALSE.

questions.q: Junior employees are described as losing the most from the absence of the office.
questions.explain: Bài viết: nhân viên mới học chủ yếu bằng cách quan sát nên "appear to lose most" → TRUE.

questions.q: Most companies now require employees to attend the office five days a week.
questions.explain: Bài không cung cấp thông tin về chính sách đi làm đủ năm ngày → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why does the writer mention a casual remark overheard at a neighbouring desk?
options: To show that office environments are frequently noisy
To illustrate how informal exchanges pass on knowledge
To criticise the prevalence of unplanned meetings in modern workplaces
To explain why managers often prefer remote work arrangements
questions.explain: Những trao đổi không kế hoạch như vậy "transmit tacit knowledge and cement relationships" → đáp án đúng: To illustrate how informal exchanges pass on knowledge.

questions.q: What do the most successful firms do, according to the passage?
options: They abolish the office completely.
They choose a policy and apply it strictly.
They decide which activities benefit from being together and plan around them.
They allow employees to choose any schedule.
questions.explain: Bài viết: họ hỏi hoạt động nào "genuinely benefit from being in the same room" và thiết kế lịch quanh đó → đáp án đúng: They decide which activities benefit from being together and plan around them.

readings.title: The Particles We Cannot See
readings.summaryVi: Vi nhựa đã được tìm thấy từ biển sâu đến cơ thể người; tác hại đối với sức khỏe vẫn chưa rõ, nên việc giảm phát thải ngay từ nguồn là hướng thận trọng hợp lý.
readings.summaryEn: Microplastics have been found from the deep sea to the human body; the health effects remain unclear, so cutting emissions at source is the sensible precaution.
readings.text:
Plastic does not disappear; it fragments. Bottles, packaging and synthetic textiles break down into ever smaller pieces, and those under five millimetres in length are known as microplastics. They have been detected in the deepest ocean trenches, in Arctic snow and, more recently and more disquietingly, in human blood, lungs and placentas.

What these particles do to living organisms is far from settled. Laboratory studies show that they can cause inflammation in cells and carry toxic chemicals on their surfaces, but the doses used often exceed those found in the environment, and extrapolating to human health is hazardous. Researchers also struggle with the sheer diversity of the material: particles differ in size, shape and chemical composition, so that conclusions about one type may not apply to another.

Given such uncertainty, some argue that alarm is premature. Others invoke the precautionary principle, the view that when an activity threatens harm, lack of conclusive proof should not delay sensible measures. Since plastic is so persistent that anything released now will remain for generations, waiting for certainty would be a gamble.

Fortunately, the measures that would reduce exposure are not especially controversial. Filters on washing machines can capture fibres from clothing, better waste management prevents litter from degrading in rivers, and redesigning products to use less plastic addresses the problem at its source. Cleaning up what is already in the environment is far harder, which is the strongest argument for acting before the evidence is complete.

questions.q: Microplastics have been found inside the human body.
questions.explain: Bài viết: đã phát hiện vi nhựa "in human blood, lungs and placentas" → TRUE.

questions.q: It has been conclusively proved that microplastics cause serious disease in humans.
questions.explain: Bài viết: tác động lên sinh vật sống "is far from settled" (còn lâu mới rõ ràng) → FALSE.

questions.q: Most microplastics in the ocean come from car tyres.
questions.explain: Bài không nêu nguồn chính của vi nhựa ở đại dương; chỉ nhắc chai, bao bì và dệt tổng hợp → NOT GIVEN.

questions.q: Why is it difficult to apply laboratory results to human health?
options: The doses used are often higher than real exposure.
The equipment in many labs lacks proper calibration.
The microplastics tend to aggregate when mixed with water.
The human body can metabolize plastic without any effect.
questions.explain: Bài viết: liều dùng trong phòng thí nghiệm "often exceed those found in the environment" → đáp án đúng: The doses used are often higher than real exposure.

questions.q: What does the precautionary principle suggest here?
options: Waiting for complete proof before acting
Ignoring the risks until they are proven
Banning all plastics immediately
Acting sensibly despite incomplete evidence
questions.explain: Bài viết: khi một hoạt động đe dọa gây hại, việc thiếu bằng chứng kết luận không nên trì hoãn biện pháp hợp lý → đáp án đúng: Acting sensibly despite incomplete evidence.
